item.title: Nagasaki Champon Noodles — Guide
item.description: Champon is Nagasaki’s most famous dish, a hearty and satisfying noodle soup born from the city’s Chinese heritage. It was created in the Meiji era by a Chinese restaurateur in Nagasaki who wanted to serve cheap, filling and nutritious meals to Chinese students — and it has been the city’s comfort food ever since. A bowl of champon combines thick, springy wheat noodles in a rich, milky-white broth made from pork bones and chicken, loaded with a generous stir-fried topping of pork, cabbage, beansprouts, kamaboko fish cake, squid, shrimp and other seafood and vegetables.
